correctness.rationale: The block phase identity F_n=[[F,DF],[FC,-DFC]] is exact. If b is even then C=I; if odd then FC=PF by the signed first-spatial-digit flip, so elimination leaves D+PDP. Its diagonal entries have magnitude 2cos(pi/(2b)). The determinant recurrence and normalization yield the asserted exponent by induction. Every Gram eigenvalue is positive and the geometric-mean bound is elementary. The standalone dependency-free checker independently evaluates finite determinants (35 cases) and parity identities (54 cases); these checks are corroborative, not infinite proof.

value.rationale: The exact finite Gram-volume law answers a natural invariant motivated by constructing finite-scale Fourier bases for two-digit Cantor measures. It identifies a crisp even/odd base transition: unitary interpolation in every even base versus an exact exponential collapse of Gram geometric mean and a rigorous instability upper bound for one canonical odd-base tower. The full parameter class b>=3 and n>=1 is classified; the claim avoids conflating this benchmark with universal limiting-frame obstructions.
